messages.content: We are developing a world-model learning paper and need a NEW MECHANISTIC operation with a broad idea, not another familiar principle renamed. Native experiments so far: truthful experience changes forecasts, but strong actors correct and all tasks succeed; correct behavior does not always repair the shared predictor. Reactor Lab finite symbolic model fitting works8/10; noisy measurement contexts cause remaining failures. Hand-supplied isolation/min32 calibration helps. Searching finite measurement programs works but costs7.37x calibration. Lazy calibration after actual task failure works7/8 vs fixed8/8; one failure refits exactly the already-falsified prediction after a reference reading changes0.01. This is a weak baseline bug, not a discovery. Generic propagation of refutations is Popper/Hempel/CEGIS, so not new either. We have discarded retellings of active experiment design, meta-learning/gradient alignment, measurement calibration, model repair retrieval(VERDI), homing, training-order commutators, and optimizer-state poisoning. General expressibility as an established framework is fine: novelty must be in an exact algorithmic operation and a meaningful failure it addresses. Propose ONE nontrivial next operator that can be implemented and falsified cheaply using native ScienceWorld/DiscoveryWorld or a small standard control task. Give one-sentence core idea, exact update equations/procedure, strongest concrete existing-algorithm baseline, why their outputs differ on the same evidence for substantive reasons, and a minimal informative experiment. Do NOT propose another template search, data weighting, replay protection, confidence threshold, cloned-model forks without distinct branch construction, or only a theorem/audit. No invented citations. Be explicit about the weakest assumption. Under700 words.
